blinding_guess.why: At this revision the package is the Qt4-era binding (PyQt4/PySide only) and re-exports the binding's whole QtGui and QtCore modules, with QtWidgets aliased to QtGui; under Qt4 the widget classes QAction, QMessageBox and QToolButton live in QtGui and QSize in QtCore, so all four element paths would resolve here. This is a guess from general Qt knowledge, not verified from allowed sources.

notes: The snapshot names none of the four symbols: a search of every file for QAction, QMessageBox, QSize and QToolButton returned no hits. python_qt_binding 0.2.19 does not declare individual classes. It imports whole binding modules and re-exports them. In binding_helper.py, _select_qt_binding (lines 49-98) tries the loaders in DEFAULT_BINDING_ORDER ['pyqt', 'pyside'] (line 53), which can be overridden via sys.SELECT_QT_BINDING / sys.SELECT_QT_BINDING_ORDER (lines 268-271). _load_pyqt imports PyQt4.<module> (line 144) and _load_pyside imports PySide.<module> (line 181) for required_modules ['QtCore', 'QtGui'] (lines 62-65) and for the optional modules. _register_binding_module (lines 101-105) registers each module both as a top-level sys.modules entry under its own name (for example 'QtGui'; the comment calls this legacy compatibility) and in QT_BINDING_MODULES. Line 90 sets QT_BINDING_MODULES['QtWidgets'] = QT_BINDING_MODULES['QtGui'] 'for forward compatibility with Qt5'. __init__.py (lines 58-60) then exposes every QT_BINDING_MODULES entry as python_qt_binding.<name>. So api:QtGui.QAction and api:QtGui.QMessageBox reach consumers through the top-level 'QtGui' module or through python_qt_binding.QtGui; api:python_qt_binding.QtGui.QToolButton goes through python_qt_binding.QtGui, and api:python_qt_binding.QtCore.QSize through python_qt_binding.QtCore. Whether each class exists in those modules depends on the installed PyQt4 or PySide QtGui/QtCore module. That content is outside the allowed sources (it is not a .msg/.srv/.action/.idl definition), so I could not determine from allowed sources whether any element is declared, and all four are in neither declares nor not_declared. The code does rely on QtGui holding widget classes: line 167 has 'from QtGui import QFileDialog', and line 90 aliases QtWidgets to QtGui. The ports are listed because the package re-exports the modules that contain these paths. msg_type, frame, units, QoS, rate and definition_id do not apply to Python API symbols and are null (QoS is also null for ROS 1). references is empty because every packet element is on the provides side.
